Use ready areas for known games
When a game with ready areas (such as GTA 6) is being played, its help box and messages are read and translated automatically. Your own extra areas take precedence.
Automatic on-screen text translation is experimental; you can turn it on in Settings.
Text boxes that appear on screen (objectives, help, messages) are found and translated in place. Counters, the map and short labels are skipped.
Translate the screen always translates everything.
Set on-screen text apart from subtitles
On-screen text keeps its own colours and place, and never looks like the subtitle box.
Each speaker\'s name and line keep their own color.
Check unchanged subtitle areas more often
When the subtitle area looks unchanged, read it again after 2 frames instead of 20. Uses more CPU.
In GTA 6, set the subtitle background to Solid. Only text on the dark blue subtitle panel will be translated.
Wait for a clearer reading when a line contains unrecognized words; the recommended delay is 0.8 seconds.

When a line looks cut off (no sentence ending, such as a mission text with a colored word), the full line is awaited for at most this long. Its effect is small: at 0 s a few more lines arrive cut off. Recommended: 0.3 s.
These waits only delay lines that were read badly; most lines are shown without waiting. A shorter wait shows those lines sooner but lets more wrong translations through.
“Watch subtitle background” is on: only text on GTA 6’s dark subtitle panel is read. Set the game’s subtitle background to Solid or turn this setting off.
Play Xbox sound on this device
During remote play, Xbox sends sound to this phone; use its speaker or connected headphones to hear the game.
Screen stays on · brightness dims automatically

Installs the translation app on your LG TV (webOS) from this phone, without a computer. The phone and the TV must be on the same Wi-Fi.
Needs LG\'s Developer Mode app on the TV and a free LG developer account. the translation app extends the developer mode session for you.
Turn on the LG TV and connect it to the phone network, or enter its network address below.
Passphrase (key saved; type it if needed)
Turn on developer mode on the TV
1. Create a free LG developer account at webostv.developer.lge.com.
2. On the TV, install the Developer Mode app from the LG Content Store, open it, sign in with your account and turn on Dev Mode Status. The TV restarts.
3. Open the Developer Mode app again and turn on Key Server. Leave the app on screen; a 6-character Passphrase appears at the bottom left.
4. Type the Passphrase above and press Install and open. The passphrase is only needed for the first install.
Developer mode stays on for at most 1000 hours. the translation app extends it by itself once a day while the phone can reach the TV.

Developer options and debugging turned on on the TV (steps 1 and 2).
A box has no HDMI input of its own, so subtitles appear on the box\'s picture, not over a PS5 connected to another input of the TV. To show them over the game, use an Android TV set itself.
Open Settings › Device Preferences › About (Google TV: Settings › System › About) and press OK seven times on Build to turn on Developer options.
In Developer options turn on USB debugging, and Network debugging if it appears.
Press the install button below, then pick the TV on the next screen.
When the TV asks Allow USB debugging, tick Always allow, then press Allow.
If it cannot connect, choose Wireless debugging and enter the address, the port and the 6-digit pairing code shown on the TV.
The app opens on the TV. Start the translation from Home and approve the pairing request on the phone.
The TV does not answer: make sure it is on and on the phone\'s network.
The debugging prompt keeps coming back: choose Always allow when you approve.
The wireless debugging port changes every time: enter the port the TV shows now.
After the TV restarts, open the translation app from Apps if it does not open by itself. If the subtitles show without a picture, pick the HDMI input from the inputs panel.
An LG TV with webOS 4 or later (2018 models and newer).
Phone and TV on the same Wi-Fi.
A free LG developer account, and the Developer Mode app from the LG Content Store on the TV.
Create a free developer account at webostv.developer.lge.com.
On the TV install Developer Mode from the LG Content Store, sign in, then turn on Dev Mode Status. The TV restarts.
Open Developer Mode again, turn on Key Server and leave the app open. A 6-character Passphrase appears at the bottom of the screen.
Press the install button below, pick the TV, type the Passphrase exactly as shown, in capital letters, then press Install and open.
The app opens on the TV. Start the translation from Home and accept, with the remote, the connection prompt that appears on the TV.
The TV does not answer: turn it on, and check that it is on the phone\'s network and Dev Mode Status is on.
The developer session (up to 1000 hours) ended and the app was removed: turn Dev Mode Status on again and reinstall. Targamgi extends the session daily while it is connected to the TV.
The Passphrase was refused: open Key Server again and type the code in capital letters as shown.
After the TV restarts, open the translation app from the app list if it does not open by itself.
A Samsung smart TV (Tizen) from 2016; 2016 to 2018 models are experimental.
Phone and TV on the same Wi-Fi: not a guest network, and no VPN.
A free Samsung account for the first-time sign-in. If your account uses Google sign-in, set a Samsung password for it first.
Open Apps and enter 1 2 3 4 5 on the remote to open Developer mode, or find it in App Settings.
Turn on Developer mode and enter this phone\'s address in Host PC IP: %1$s, then confirm.
Restart the TV fully: hold the power button until the Samsung logo appears (about 5 seconds), or unplug it for 30 seconds.
Press the install button below, then pick the TV.
Sign in with your Samsung account in the window that opens (first install only).
The app installs and opens on the TV. Start the translation from Home and approve the pairing request on the phone.
The TV does not accept the phone: check that Host PC IP is the phone\'s current address, which changes when it reconnects to the network, then restart the TV fully.
Develop Mode should show at the top of the Apps screen after the restart; if it does not, repeat steps 1 to 3.
The TV is off or on another network: turn it on, join the phone\'s network and try again.
Open the translation app from Apps; disable Anynet+ if the TV repeatedly switches to HDMI 1.
Connect the other device to the phone network, excluding guest networks.
A web browser on that device; no app to install.
The translation running on the phone: the page is served only while it runs. To try without a console use Try demo mode.
Start the translation from Home on the phone.
Open the browser on the other device (LG: Home, then Web Browser; Samsung: the Internet app).
Type the address shown below into the address bar exactly as it is, keeping capital and small letters; or scan the code with a phone or tablet camera.
Tap the page for full screen, and bookmark it to reopen it quickly.
The page does not open: check that the translation is running on the phone, both devices are on the same network and VPN is off, then reload the page.
The address stopped working: the phone\'s address changes when it reconnects to the network, and the key changes after Renew access key. Read the address here again.
Browsers on older TVs may not display the page correctly; try another browser or use the phone screen.
The phone on the same Wi-Fi as the PS5: not a guest network, and no VPN.
No TV and no extra app are needed.
Pick this card, then press Continue.
Start the translation from Home; the large subtitle screen opens by itself.
Put the phone sideways next to the TV or monitor, where you can read it without it covering the game.
Keep the phone on a charger; continuous translation drains the battery.
If the translation stops when the screen turns off, exclude the app from battery saving in the phone settings.
To show subtitles on a TV as well, pick Both below.
